newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan stocks end 4.99 pct up in 1997 record.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan stocks end 4.99 pct up in 1997 record.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended 4.99 percent up, a record in 1997 so far, on Sunday on bullish sentiment in almost all blue chips, a day before pro-business Nawaz Sharif's oath-taking as prime minister, dealers said.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index ended 81.79 points, or 4.99 percent, up at 1,721.07, more than this year's previous record of 4.11 percent on February 2. Gainers led losers 330 to 37 in a turnover of 87.9 million shares compared to Thursday's 49.6 million.
The sentiment is still strong and the index is likely to go up despite Monday's settlement day, one dealer said.
Foreign and local institutions unloaded some stocks but retail clients bought them, the dealer said. "Investors hope Sharif will have pro-business policies."
Engro Chemical rose 10 rupees to 160, PSO 6.00 to 305, Dewan Salman 3.05 to 44.25, Shell Pakistan 2.00 to 165, HUBCO 1.00 to 41.25, PTCL 0.30 to 34.30 and Fauji Fertilizer 4.50 to 88.
